item.title: Why Trump saved Jensen Huang
item.description:
The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia means the Trump administration is prioritizing the stock market over national security.
This episode was produced by Avishay Artsy and Peter Balonon-Rosen, edited by Amina Al-Sadi, fact-checked by Gabriel Dunatov and Hady Mawajdeh, engineered by David Tatasciore and Bridger Dunnagan, and hosted by Noel King.
President Donald Trump greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outside the White House on Sept. 29, 2026. Photo by Kevin Dietsch via Getty Images.

item.title: Drowning in credit card debt
item.description:
The US economy is built on consumption but a new proposed cap on credit card interest rates could curb that.
This episode was produced by Kelli Wessinger, edited by Amina Al-Sadi, fact-checked by Gabriel Dunatov, engineered by David Tatasciore and Bridger Dunnagan, and hosted by Noel King.

item.title: The rise of kidults
item.description:
Adults with no kids now make up the majority of toy sales. It’s good for the industry — and their own well-being.
This episode was produced by Peter Balonon-Rosen, edited by Avishay Artsy, fact-checked by Melissa Hirsch, engineered by Bridger Dunnagan, and hosted by Jonquilyn Hill.
A man fills holes on a wall with Lego bricks during a workshop at the Matadero Cultural Center in Madrid. Photo by Dani Pozo/AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: Democrats audition for 2028
item.itunes:title: Democrats audition for 2028
item.itunes:author: Vox
item.itunes:subtitle: In a candid conversation, US Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) explains why voters haven’t necessarily fallen in love with the Democratic brand, why the party must center people over politics, and how the path to power runs through the South.
item.content:encoded:
In a candid conversation, US Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) explains why voters haven’t necessarily fallen in love with the Democratic brand, why the party must center people over politics, and how the path to power runs through the South. 

This show was edited by Kasia Broussalian, fact checked by Sarah Schweppe, mixed by Shannon Mahoney, video edited by Christopher Snyder, and hosted by Astead Herndon.

Photo caption: US Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) reacts while taking the stage to speak during the What's Next summit at Mission Ballroom on November 13, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. Photo by Mark Makela/Getty Images.

You can also watch this episode on youtube.com/vox. Listen to Today, Explained ad-free by becoming a Vox Member: vox.com/members. New Vox members get $20 off their membership right now.

item.title: Is GTA VI the last of its kind?
item.description:
Ah shit, here we go again. Grand Theft Auto VI might be the biggest game release of all time. And the last of a dying breed.
This episode was produced by Dustin DeSoto, edited by Jolie Myers, fact-checked by Gabriel Dunatov, engineered by David Tatasciore and Bridger Dunnagan, and hosted by Sean Rameswaram.
The Edinburgh headquarters of Rockstar North sports a huge mural of characters from Grand Theft Auto 6 in Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom. Photo by Ken Jack via Getty Images.

item.title: Is Katseye ok?
item.description:
The girl group is one of the biggest pop music acts in the world. But two members are on hiatus, another is performing through a concussion, and fans are wondering if it’s all worth it.
This episode was produced by Hady Mawajdeh, edited by Jolie Myers, fact-checked by Gabriel Dunatov, engineered by David Tatasciore, and hosted by Sean Rameswaram.
Lara Raj, Megan Skiendiel, Daniela Avanzini and Yoonchae Jeong from KATSEYE perform on NBC's "Today" at Rockefeller Plaza on Aug. 14, 2026 in New York City. Photo by Patricia Schlein/Star Max/GC Images via Getty Images.
